real_s3.explanation: The unit responds to the head and neck/shoulder region of furry mammals, mostly dogs, and is strongest when the head is seen from the front and fills a moderate share of the frame (between a quarter and half of the image) with furry ears and the neck area clearly visible. It extends more weakly to other furry mammals.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to the head and neck/shoulder region of furry mammals, mostly dogs, and is strongest when the head is seen from the front and fills a moderate share of the frame (between a quarter and half of the image) with furry ears and the neck area clearly visible. It extends more weakly to other furry mammals.
parsed.evidence: Neck/shoulder visibility is the strongest separator (separation percentile 99; clearly visible d +0.62, partly visible d -0.68 at percentile 1), and a moderate head/upper-body size (d +0.75, percentile 98), frontal view (+0.44) and furry ears (+0.36) also raise activity. Fur length (Q4) and dog-versus-other-mammal (Q1, Q7) barely matter within classes, and since top classes are almost all dogs plus a meerkat and wolf, the 'related mammals' extension rests mostly on the original description.
parsed.missing_data: Activation maps showing where in the image the unit fires (neck/cheek fur versus the whole head), plus photos of non-dog furry mammals and of fur textures without heads, to test whether the unit is about head-and-neck framing or fur texture itself.

null_s2.explanation: The unit responds mainly to dogs, especially photos where the dog's neck/shoulder area beside the face and its furry ears are clearly visible. It responds less, or at most weakly, to other furry mammals.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds mainly to dogs, especially photos where the dog's neck/shoulder area beside the face and its furry ears are clearly visible. It responds less, or at most weakly, to other furry mammals.
parsed.evidence: Within the top classes, dog photos are more active than non-dog photos (d +0.23, percentile 98), while other furry mammals are less active (d -0.35, percentile 2), so the proposed extension to non-dog mammals is not supported within these classes. A clearly visible neck/shoulder (d +0.15, percentile 83) and furry ears (d +0.16) help modestly, whereas head view and fur length explain almost nothing.
parsed.missing_data: Activations on photos from a broad set of non-dog mammal classes (hyena, monkey, squirrel, mink) compared with non-animal classes, and box-location data, would show whether the extension to other furry mammals is real.
